target_customer: Teams and developers whose AI agents need to buy APIs, tools and other paid services with spending controls and audit trails
problem: Agents cannot easily pay for services: computer use is brittle, card permissions are hard to manage and each agent needs its own accounts.
business_model: usage-based agent wallet and marketplace, company says zero markup

founders.name: Aryah Oztanir
education: University of North Carolina, dropped out (per the YC launch post)
founders.background_notes: YC page gives no further bio.

founders.name: Ajay Misra
education: University of North Carolina, dropped out (per the YC launch post)
founders.background_notes: YC bio: enjoys training models. The launch post says the founders met finance students during internships; employers not named.

competitors.name: Skyfire
competitors.what: KYAPay identity and payment protocol for agents, demonstrated with Visa Intelligent Commerce

competitors.name: Crossmint
competitors.what: virtual Visa and Mastercard cards and programmable wallets for agents

competitors.name: OpenRouter
competitors.what: model gateway with prepaid credits and per-key spend limits, the model the tagline borrows from

technical_complexity.rationale: Spend controls, quotes, audit logs and many provider integrations are ordinary engineering; payments compliance and provider coverage add difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: A catalog of 8,416 tools from 549 providers (company claim) helps, but Stripe, Crossmint and others offer agent payment rails.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Stripe launched a Link agent wallet by mid 2026 per trade coverage, entering the same wedge after o11's batch.

market_need_then: Agentic commerce was a hot theme in late 2025 and 2026 with Stripe, Visa and startups building rails, but real agent spending volume was small.

branding.domain_note: Uses o11.ai; no purchase history found.

identity.visual_style: minimal layout with short bold headlines and a wallet at sunset photo

brand_strength.rationale: Short name but o11 reads like 'ol1' or o-eleven, easy to misspell and a numeronym style; no press on the brand found.

pivots.from: AI agent inside Excel, PowerPoint, Word and Google Workspace for finance workflows (YC launch post)
pivots.to: wallet for AI agents to pay for APIs and services
pivots.why: not stated by a source; the directory tagline and site now describe the wallet

outcome_analysis: o11 is an active Winter 2026 company that moved from a finance-focused office-app agent to an agent payments wallet. It has no exit and no verified round. The site lists notable backers, and the wedge faces large players such as Stripe that entered in 2026. Outcome is not yet determinable.
notes: Aggregators disagree on funding: one lists $2,000,000 total, another $500K; unverified, so no round recorded. The o11.ai site lists backers including Y Combinator, LeapYear, Spot VC, Accel, Scout, 645 Ventures, Paul Graham, CRV, Eight Capital and Phosphor Capital without amounts; the 645 Ventures portfolio URL returned 404. Funding date and stage unknown. Funding completeness pass: one round recorded from Caplight (seed, 2026-01, 500K), matching Neuronfeed's 500K figure; it rests on aggregators only and is probably the standard YC deal. Everydev lists 2M, VCBacked dates a seed to 2026-04, Employbl calls it pre-seed; unresolved conflicts. No press release found.
